model_annotations.Bulgarian: The diagram is a circular chart that compares different categories of characters, with a central cluster labeled "Virtual Characters" and an outer ring containing various character types. There are eight distinct categories represented: "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," "Game Characters," "Real Characters," "Custom Characters," and a group of five subcategories—“Scientists,” “Artists,” “Athletes,” “Writers,” “Musicians,” “Actors,” and “Influencers”—that are grouped together in the outer ring. The central "Virtual Characters" section is the largest, colored in light blue, and occupies a significant portion of the inner circle. The "Real Characters" section is colored green and is smaller than the virtual category but larger than the "Custom Characters" segment, which is colored red. The outer ring is divided into eight segments, each corresponding to a character type, with "Comic Characters" being the largest outer segment, followed by "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," "Game Characters," and the group of real-life roles (Scientists, Artists, Athletes, Writers, Musicians, Actors, Influencers) collectively forming the smallest portion. The labels for each category are placed adjacent to their respective segments, and the chart does not include a separate legend or explicit percentage values within the segments, though the relative sizes of the sections are visually distinguishable. No segment is visually emphasized through expansion or separation.
model_annotations.English: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of character types across various media and categories, with segments categorized by their source or origin. The chart is composed of multiple slices, each representing a different type of character, and is labeled with text indicating the category. The largest segment, colored light blue, is labeled "Virtual Characters" and occupies a significant portion of the chart. Surrounding this central segment are several other categories: "Comic Characters," "Movie Characters," "Teleplay Characters," "Novel Characters," and "Game Characters," all of which are part of a larger light blue ring, suggesting they are subcategories or related to virtual characters. On the right side of the chart, a smaller, distinct section labeled "Real Characters" is shown in green, with further subdivisions into "Custom Characters," "Scientists," "Artists," "Athletes," "Writers," "Musicians," "Actors," and "Influencers," each represented by a different colored slice. The chart uses color coding to differentiate between categories, with the "Real Characters" section and its subcategories using shades of green and red, while the "Virtual Characters" section and its subcategories use shades of blue. The labels are positioned outside the pie chart, with lines pointing to their respective slices, and the chart appears to be arranged in a circular layout with no apparent order to the segments.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm zeigt eine visuelle Klassifizierung von Charakteren in verschiedene Kategorien, wobei die Segmente durch Farben und Beschriftungen unterschieden werden. Es umfasst insgesamt neun verschiedene Kategorien, die in einem Kreisdiagramm dargestellt sind. Im Zentrum befindet sich ein blauer Bereich mit der Bezeichnung „Virtual Characters“, der den größten Anteil des Diagramms einnimmt. Um diesen herum sind weitere Kategorien angeordnet: „Comic Characters“ (hellblau), „Movie Characters“ (hellblau), „Teleplay Characters“ (hellblau), „Novel Characters“ (hellblau) und „Game Characters“ (hellblau), die alle in einer hellblauen Farbpalette gehalten sind und sich im äußeren Ring des Diagramms befinden. Im rechten Bereich des Diagramms sind sechs weitere Kategorien in einem kleineren, inneren Ring angeordnet: „Custom Characters“ (rot), „Real Characters“ (grün), „Scientists“ (rosa), „Artists“ (rosa), „Athletes“ (rosa), „Writers“ (rosa), „Musicians“ (rosa), „Actors“ (rosa) und „Influencers“ (rosa), wobei die Farben von Rot über Grün bis hin zu Rosa variieren. Die Beschriftungen sind direkt in die jeweiligen Segmente eingefügt, und es gibt keine sichtbare Legende. Die Anordnung der Segmente scheint nicht nach einer klaren numerischen Reihenfolge, sondern nach thematischen Gruppen zu erfolgen, wobei die „Virtual Characters“ als zentraler und dominanter Bereich hervorgehoben sind.
